content:
This appears to be a Sumerian creation myth or cosmogonic text. Here's my translation:

1. From long ago, when heaven and earth were [created]
2. From long ago, when night from heaven and earth was [created]
3. From [long] ago, when the year/destinies were [determined]
4. When the Anunna-gods were born
5. When Ama-Dinana possessed sovereignty
6. When Ama-Dinana was distributed throughout heaven and earth
7. When Ama-Dinana [...] was made to give birth, was born
8. When the gods' food rations [...] were bound to their dwelling places
9. The numerous gods stood at their assigned work, the lesser gods bore the labor
10. The gods who dig canals, their dirt/excavated earth they kept piling up
11. The gods who grind, they set their lives/breath to speech
12. At that time, broad wisdom (and) intelligence existed among the numerous gods
13. Enki, in the Abzu, the deep well of subterranean waters, the place where no god looks into its heart
14. He lay on his resting place and sleep would not depart
15. The gods wept, lamentations took place, they cried
16. The one lying in the holy place, from his resting place would not arise
17. Namma, the mother who gave birth to all the numerous gods
18. Brought the gods' tears to her son
19. "You are lying down, you are sleeping"
20. [...] you do not arise
21. The gods fashioned by your hand [...] are destroying themselves

Note: This text describes the primordial creation of the universe and the birth of the gods, leading to a labor dispute among the gods that requires Enki's intervention. Some portions are damaged or unclear, indicated by brackets and question marks.
